summary: Whatcom County 20-foot L-4 tower built 1935, a 1942 AWS spotting post, abandoned 1959; remnants seen on a 2014 visit, nothing confirmed since.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: The register says it was abandoned in 1959 and is gone. A Forest Lookouts page says destroyed, with no date. WillhiteWeb found remnants on a 2014 visit.

staffing.status: AWS spotting use, activated March 21 to August 24, 1942

access.note: Off-trail route on Forest Service land, starting from FR 12 and an abandoned road with a blockade. No closure found in the sources.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb gives 1.8 miles round trip and 846 feet of cumulative gain, with a creek crossing, a lava field and a steep forested hill. The tower is gone, so there is nothing to climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it Sulphur Point; Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb call it Sulphur Butte. The shared 1935 panorama date (September 11) and the 2,262-foot elevation support one site.
The register and FireLookout.com say abandoned in 1959 and gone; Forest Lookouts says destroyed with no date. The story reports both.

sources.title: Sulphur Butte Lookout - Baker Lake Sights

notes_for_editor: Name conflict: the register says Sulphur Point; Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb say Sulphur Butte. We treat them as one site on the strength of the matching September 11, 1935 panorama date and 2,262-foot elevation; the Forest Lookouts page itself lists the site as Sulphur Butte (point). The sources never expand the acronym AWS, so the story leaves it unexpanded and drops 'wartime', which the sources do not use. 'Burned timbers' is a 2014 photo caption, with no fire date, so no fire event is recorded. The most recent account is the 2014 visit. The 'public' access level is inferred from Forest Service land and the absence of any closure notice. The brief's 1935 build and 2020 registration checked out; the brief's 'tower' kind is supported.
